newsitem.title: USA: Homeowners join power market competition bandwagon.
newsitem.headline: Homeowners join power market competition bandwagon.

text.p: United Homeowners Association said Tuesday iit joined with a coalition of eight utilities to press Congress to make states open local power markets to competition by 2001.
Up to now, the loudest voices for customer choice have been manufacturers seeking to slash their electricity bills.

"We're in there to make sure that residential customers, who in the aggregate are probably the biggest electricity consumers, are treated fairly and don't get lost in the battle between the big users and our elected officials," said Jordan Clark, president of United Homeowners Association.

Advocates for retired people and the poor have warned that homeowners could end up shouldering higher rates to cover the unprofitable investments of utilities that lose industrial customers as they bargain for cheap electricity.

The counsel to the Democrats on the House Commerce Committee, the committee leading the effort to dismantle utility monopolies, recently said lawmakers would want to hear from all consumers before they moved to pass a bill.
United Homeowners Association has 52,000 individual members out of 65 million U.S. homeowners, and is starting to reach out to local homeowner associations, Clark said.
"Our constituency has more political power on the aggregate," Clark said. "We want to make sure the consitutents back home get the real story."

Clark said that issues such as who should carry the costs of utilities' stranded investments and access to local distribution lines would take time to resolve, but it was essential for homeowners to be involved.

"It's an issue where we have lot of experience via telecom deregulation," he said, referring to the five year process that led up to passage last year of a bill to open local telephone markets to competition.
